evaluated.name: Self-Funded R&D Intensity
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible investment carried on internal cash flow is credible innovation, whereas equity-funded intangible spending is contaminated by market-timed issuance; the spread between R&D intensity and equity-issuance intensity isolates the productive component and earns positive abnormal returns.
evaluated.reasoning: R&D intensity alone is a known positive-return characteristic and share issuance alone is a known negative one, but the interaction matters because the same R&D dollar is priced very differently when it is bankrolled by new equity sold at a high valuation. Ranking both channels before differencing makes the two themes comparable in units and keeps the signal robust to scaling outliers. COALESCE treats non-reporting firms as zero R&D, which is the standard economic convention and preserves broad coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Debt-Disciplined Innovation Funding
evaluated.hypothesis: Among R&D-intensive firms, those tilting external funding toward debt rather than equity are monitored, cash-flow-confident innovators, while equity-tilted R&D funders are exploiting overvaluation; the product of R&D intensity and the debt-minus-equity funding mix identifies productive intangible financing.
evaluated.reasoning: Debt issuance requires servicing capacity and creditor scrutiny, so it is a costly signal when intangible assets provide little collateral, whereas equity issuance is cheapest precisely when the stock is rich. The multiplicative form makes the funding-mix tilt matter most where intangible investment is large, which is the exact conditioning the economic story requires.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Payout-Backed Knowledge Capital
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that simultaneously return capital to shareholders and sustain a large stock of accumulated R&D are signaling that their intangible capital is internally financeable and undervalued; this joint configuration should outperform intangible-heavy firms that must absorb outside capital.
evaluated.reasoning: Negative net external financing (repurchases plus dividends) is a credible statement that management sees the shares as cheap, and it is most informative when the firm also owns a deep, hard-to-value knowledge stock that markets systematically underprice. Five-year cumulative R&D captures the intangible capital state rather than a single noisy annual flow, and SUMRANK combines the two themes with equal, outlier-resistant weight.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Externally Financed Goodwill Buildup
evaluated.hypothesis: Purchased intangibles (goodwill) created while the firm is simultaneously raising large amounts of debt and equity reflect overpayment for acquired intangible assets funded by cheap capital, and such firms subsequently underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: Goodwill is the accounting residual of acquisition prices, so its growth is a direct measure of how much the buyer paid above identifiable value; when that purchase is financed externally rather than from internal cash, agency and market-timing motives dominate and later write-downs follow. The multiplicative form is essential because organic goodwill-light growth or financing unaccompanied by acquisitions carries no such implication.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Issuance Against Fading Intangible Productivity
evaluated.hypothesis: Equity issuance is overvaluation-driven rather than investment-driven when the revenue productivity of the firm's existing intangible base is deteriorating; issuers with declining sales-per-intangible-dollar should earn the most negative subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: If intangible capital is still converting into revenue at an improving rate, new equity plausibly funds a positive-NPV innovation pipeline, but a multi-year decline in intangible productivity means the firm is capitalizing soft assets that no longer generate sales while tapping the market. The five-year TREND supplies the needed state-deterioration concept that a one-year change would measure too noisily, and the product form makes the productivity trend bite only where issuance is actually occurring.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Direction-Signed External Intangible Funding
evaluated.hypothesis: The same amount of external capital raised is good news when intangible investment intensity is rising (funds are being deployed into innovation) and bad news when intangible intensity is falling (funds are being raised opportunistically), so signing financing volume by the direction of R&D intensity separates productive from timed issuance.
evaluated.reasoning: This directly implements the economic story as a sign-switch rather than an additive blend: identical financing intensity maps to opposite predictions depending on whether the intangible investment program is expanding or contracting. Using SIGN of the change in R&D-to-sales avoids letting the magnitude of a volatile ratio dominate, while the ranked financing intensity supplies the economically meaningful scale of the interaction.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Dilution-Adjusted R&D Intensity
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible investment sustained without shareholder dilution is productive innovation, whereas intangible spending accompanied by share-count expansion reflects market-timed equity funding; measuring dilution from shares outstanding rather than the cash-flow-statement issuance item captures the same economics for the whole cross-section.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-0 winner used the same rank-difference logic but was restricted to firms reporting sstk, capping coverage at 0.127 and thinning the extreme portfolios, which is the most likely cause of its weak alpha t-stat relative to its 4.8 FMB t-stat. Share-count growth is available for essentially all firms and captures all dilution channels (secondary offerings, equity-financed deals, option exercise), so this isolates the coverage design choice while holding the mechanism fixed.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Industry-Neutral Self-Funded Innovation
evaluated.hypothesis: Within an industry, the firm that funds its intangible program internally rather than through equity and debt issuance is the one whose innovation is genuinely value-creating; across industries the same comparison mostly reproduces sector R&D norms and financing conventions, which FF5 factors already span.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-0 winner's large FMB slope but weak FF5 alpha t-stat suggests the long-short leg was a pharma/tech versus financials-utilities bet whose systematic component is absorbed by the factor model. Ranking both themes inside industry should preserve the cross-sectional slope while converting it into a cleaner, better-diversified spread, and it also tests total external financing (equity plus debt) rather than equity alone.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Net-Financing-Free Knowledge Capital
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(dltt, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A deep accumulated knowledge stock that was built while both equity and debt financing were shrinking identifies self-financing innovators whose intangible capital the market underprices; the same knowledge stock built on simultaneous equity and debt expansion reflects externally subsidized, overvaluation-driven investment.
evaluated.reasoning: Gen-0's Payout-Backed Knowledge Capital tested the same idea but proxied "no external funding" with repurchases and dividends, which selects large mature payers and gave a negative alpha; net changes in shares and in total debt measure contraction of external capital directly and include young non-payers. Five-year cumulative R&D captures the intangible state rather than a noisy annual flow, and equal-weight nested SUMRANK avoids the multiplicative structures that failed in gen 0.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Intangible Capital Delivered Per Share
evaluated.hypothesis: The only intangible investment that matters to an incumbent shareholder is the amount surviving dilution, so growth in intangible capital per share separates financing that actually bought innovation from financing that merely transferred claims; firms increasing intangible capital per share earn positive abnormal returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes the interaction from an additive comparison of two ranks to a single per-share intensity, so the financing theme enters as the deflator of the intangible theme rather than as a competing score — a structurally different test of the same story. Combining booked intangibles with three-year cumulative R&D gives one economically complete intangible capital measure, and the one-year growth makes the signal about newly delivered capital rather than about the level of R&D intensity.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Externally Financed Intangible Acquisition
evaluated.hypothesis: Balance-sheet intangibles grow mainly through acquisitions, and when that growth coincides with heavy equity and debt issuance the firm is paying up for other companies' intangibles with cheap outside capital, which predicts subsequent write-downs and low returns.
evaluated.reasoning: Gen-0's goodwill version had a coherent FMB slope (-2.80) but a dead long-short leg, consistent with the MUL structure making the signal near-zero for the vast majority of firms and leaving the portfolio extremes unstable. Replacing the product with an additive SUMRANK gives a continuous, well-populated score, and using total intangibles rather than goodwill alone broadens the acquired-intangible measure.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Innovation With Unused Debt Capacity
evaluated.hypothesis: Because intangible assets are poor collateral, an R&D-intensive firm that has chosen to carry little debt retains real financing capacity and is not investing under distress pressure; the market underprices such firms relative to intangible-heavy firms whose innovation is already levered.
evaluated.reasoning: All prior proposals used financing flows; this one uses the financing state (stock of debt), so it tests whether the interaction operates through capital-structure capacity rather than through the timing of new issues. It also has near-universal coverage because it needs only xrd, dltt, dlc and at, which addresses the sparsity that plagued the flow-based archive.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Triple-Channel Self-Financed Innovation
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Productive intangible financing is identified jointly by three conditions — substantial intangible investment, no shareholder dilution, and unused debt capacity — because a firm meeting all three is funding innovation from internal resources and retains options, while intangible-heavy firms that are both diluting and levered are funding innovation on terms set by outside capital.
evaluated.reasoning: Dilution and leverage state were the two strongest portfolio channels in gen 1 but were each tested in isolation against R&D intensity; combining them tests whether their information is complementary rather than redundant. Equal-weight nested SUMRANK keeps the additive structure that has worked while ensuring no single channel drives the extreme portfolios, which should stabilize the long-short composition.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Persistently Undiluted Innovation
evaluated.hypothesis: Whether intangible investment is genuinely self-funded is a multi-year property of financing policy, not a one-year event; R&D-intensive firms with three years of low average dilution are credibly internally financed, while a single clean year can simply reflect issuance timing.
evaluated.reasoning: This isolates one design choice — the horizon of the financing channel — against the gen-1 winner while holding the intangible channel and the rank-difference structure fixed. If the smoothed version improves both the FMB slope and the alpha t-stat, the mechanism is a persistent financing-policy state; if it degrades, the effect is driven by recent issuance events and future work should stay at annual frequency.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Margin-Funded Innovation
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The economically relevant question is whether the firm's own gross margin can pay for its intangible program; innovators with high gross profitability and no dilution are funding R&D internally, whereas equally R&D-intensive firms with thin margins must sell equity and are the market-timing candidates.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has proxied "internal funding" only negatively (absence of issuance), never positively by the firm's actual cash-generating capacity; gross profit is the one internal-funds measure available in the intangibles menu and is known to be the most persistent profitability signal. This tests whether the dilution effect is really a funding-capacity effect, which would explain why pure payout-based proxies in gen 0 failed on old, low-growth firms.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Levered Purchased-Intangible Balance Sheet
evaluated.hypothesis: A balance sheet that is simultaneously heavy in goodwill and heavy in liabilities embeds unrecognized impairment risk against fixed claims: the acquired intangibles were paid for with borrowed money, and equity holders bear the writedown, so such firms earn low subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: All prior bearish proposals used financing and intangible *flows*, and their spreads were absorbed by the FF5 investment factor, leaving zero alpha despite strong FMB slopes; a levels-based configuration of the same story is much less collinear with asset growth. It also tests the acquired-intangible channel (goodwill) against the internally-generated channel (R&D) that has been dominating, which is the key economic distinction in the theme.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Innovation Minus Net Debt Issuance
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible investment funded by fresh borrowing is a leveraged bet on soft assets that cannot be liquidated, so R&D intensity net of contemporaneous net debt issuance identifies innovation the firm can actually sustain through a funding shock.
evaluated.reasoning: Gen 1 showed the debt channel produces the largest alpha (4.5%) but almost no cross-sectional slope when measured as a leverage *level*, which suggests the level is a noisy, industry-driven proxy; the annual net-issuance *flow* is the decision variable and should restore the FMB slope if the mechanism is about funding choices rather than static capital structure. Paired with signal 1, this tells us whether to build later refinements on debt stocks or debt flows.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Four-Channel Internally Financed Innovation
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Productive intangible financing requires both the ability to pay (gross margin) and the absence of outside claims on the innovation (no dilution, little debt); stacking funding capacity with funding claims should identify self-financing innovators more sharply than either enhancement alone.
evaluated.reasoning: Gross margin raised the cross-sectional slope while leverage state raised the alpha, and the two describe distinct economics — internal cash generation versus who owns the claim on it — so they are unlikely to be redundant. This is the direct consolidation test of the archive's two best refinements and will tell us which axis to keep in the final signal.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Knowledge Capital Per Dollar Of Investor Capital
evaluated.hypothesis: The efficiency with which supplied outside capital has been converted into an accumulated knowledge stock is the cleanest measure of productive intangible financing: firms holding a large R&D stock per dollar of equity plus debt capital have built innovation cheaply, while firms with little knowledge stock per financed dollar absorbed capital without creating intangible assets.
evaluated.reasoning: Every archive winner compares two separately ranked channels; this instead deflates the intangible stock by the total capital investors have actually committed, so the interaction is structural rather than additive and is not mechanically an R&D-intensity sort. Five-year cumulative R&D matches the stock concept in the denominator, and winsorizing controls the small-capital-base outliers that destroyed the FMB slope of the gen-1 per-share version.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Undiluted Innovation Acceleration
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm ramping up R&D intensity while keeping its share count flat is committing internal resources to a newly attractive opportunity set, whereas a firm ramping R&D on the back of new shares is spending other people's money raised at a favorable price.
evaluated.reasoning: Every successful archive signal measures the intangible theme as a *level* of intensity, which risks being an R&D-premium restatement; this isolates the intangible-channel flow while holding the financing channel and rank-difference structure fixed. If the growth version retains the alpha, the mechanism is about new investment decisions rather than about static innovation intensity, which matters for how we build the final signal.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Dilution By Cash-Burning Innovators
evaluated.hypothesis: The overvaluation-driven issuance case is concentrated in firms whose R&D spending exceeds their entire gross profit: these firms cannot self-fund, so heavy dilution reflects a window of favorable pricing rather than a validated investment program, and they underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's bearish signals have failed because they sorted the whole cross-section on flows that FF5's investment factor spans; this instead switches on a hard economic solvency condition (R&D above gross profit) and only then reads dilution, which targets exactly the population where market timing is feasible. The indicator makes it a true conditional rather than the multiplicative rank blends that failed in gen 0, because the gate is a discrete state, not a second ranked score.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Debt Against Non-Intangible Collateral
evaluated.hypothesis: Leverage is only as safe as the liquidatable assets behind it; firms whose debt is large relative to assets excluding booked intangibles have financed soft, non-collateralizable assets with hard claims and bear elevated distress and impairment risk, earning low returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs the gen-2 levered-goodwill failure by replacing an additive composite of two levels — whose relation to returns was non-monotone (FMB t=+0.60) — with a single continuous collateral-coverage ratio that should be monotone across the cross-section. It is also economically the mirror of the winning long side: intangible assets are attractive when equity-financed and dangerous when debt-financed.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Innovation With Stable Financing Policy
evaluated.hypothesis: Innovators whose share count follows a smooth path are funding intangible investment from a stable internal source, while innovators with volatile dilution are opportunistically tapping equity markets whenever conditions permit, which signals dependence on sentiment rather than on project quality.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has measured the financing channel only by the level or three-year average of dilution; the second moment is a distinct economic concept — reliance on episodic market access — and may capture market timing that averages out in the mean. Keeping the same rank-difference structure isolates this new financing statistic against the established R&D-intensity channel.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Rank-Stabilized Knowledge Capital Efficiency
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that have accumulated a large knowledge stock per dollar of investor-supplied capital have converted external financing into innovation efficiently and are underpriced; the economic content is the ordering of this efficiency, not the extreme magnitudes of the raw ratio.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a deliberate diagnostic on gen 3's outsized result: a monotone rank transform preserves the economic ordering while removing the influence of near-zero and negative capital denominators, so comparing the two tells us whether the 54.5% alpha is a genuine efficiency premium or a magnitude artifact of a few tail firms. It should simultaneously repair the weak FMB slope, since the cross-sectional regression is then run on a bounded regressor.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Knowledge Stock Against Total Claims
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible capital that dwarfs the firm's total outside claims represents innovation the shareholders own outright, whereas a small knowledge stock relative to large liabilities means the financing raised went to obligations rather than to innovation.
evaluated.reasoning: Total liabilities is strictly positive for essentially all firms, so this variant of the capital-efficiency mechanism cannot flip sign or explode the way an equity-plus-debt denominator can, isolating the robustness of the denominator choice. If the alpha and Sharpe of the gen-3 ratio largely survive here, the mechanism is real; if it collapses, the earlier result was driven by negative-equity distress cases.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Capital-Efficient Innovation With Margins
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(ceq, ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The strongest form of productive intangible financing combines three properties: a knowledge stock built cheaply relative to capital supplied, gross margins able to sustain it, and no need for fresh dilution; each addresses a different reason a high R&D stock might be unprofitable.
evaluated.reasoning: The two best-performing families in the archive — the capital-efficiency ratio (highest alpha and Sharpe) and the margin-plus-dilution composite (highest FMB slope, t=5.48) — have never been combined, and SUMRANK ranks the ratio internally so its tail behavior cannot dominate the score. This is the consolidation candidate that could deliver strong cross-sectional and portfolio evidence at once.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Successfully Funded Constrained Innovators
evaluated.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(SUB(COALESCE(xrd, 0), SUB(sale, cogs)), 0), SUMRANK(GROWTH(csho, 1), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Among firms whose R&D exceeds their entire gross profit, access to equity is the binding constraint, so raising capital is a certification event: heavily R&D-intensive burners that succeed in funding themselves outperform, because the alternative is curtailing innovation.
evaluated.reasoning: Gen 3 tested this exact population expecting underperformance and got the opposite (alpha +2.4%, t=2.06, Sharpe 0.79), which is direct evidence that dilution is good news precisely where internal funds cannot cover intangible investment. This version keeps the discrete solvency gate but scores gated firms on both the amount of funding obtained and the intensity of the innovation being funded, sharpening the certification interpretation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Dilution-Funded Innovation Ramp
evaluated.hypothesis: When rising R&D intensity and share issuance occur together, the equity raised is visibly being deployed into an expanding innovation program, which the market underreacts to; when R&D intensity rises without any funding, the ramp is more likely a margin collapse than a deliberate investment.
evaluated.reasoning: Gen 3's rank *difference* between R&D acceleration and dilution earned a reliably negative alpha (t=-2.91), which implies the additive combination should be the profitable orientation and makes this a decisive test of the state-dependence rather than a cosmetic variant. Using DELTA of the R&D-to-sales ratio instead of GROWTH keeps firms with zero prior R&D in the sample, tripling the coverage that crippled the earlier version (0.050).
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Goodwill Intensity Inside Levered Firms
evaluated.hypothesis: Goodwill is only dangerous when it sits on a levered balance sheet: with debt above roughly thirty percent of assets, an impairment of acquired intangibles wipes out equity value, so goodwill intensity predicts low returns only within levered firms.
evaluated.reasoning: The two bearish attempts so far generated reliable FF5 alphas (t≈-3.1) with flat FMB slopes, the signature of a relation that exists only in a tail of the joint distribution and is therefore non-monotone across the full cross-section. Gating on a discrete leverage state and ranking goodwill only inside that state converts the tail effect into a monotone score, which should let the cross-sectional slope finally align with the portfolio evidence.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Five-Channel Financed Innovation Quality
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(ceq, ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Productive intangible financing is jointly identified by knowledge capital built cheaply per dollar of investor capital, gross margins that can sustain it, absence of dilution, and unused debt capacity; each channel removes a different reason a knowledge-rich firm might still be a poor investment.
evaluated.reasoning: The capital-efficiency channel carries the archive's highest Sharpe but is non-monotone alone, while the four-channel stack carries the highest alpha t-stat with a moderate FMB slope, so ranking efficiency inside the stack should import its long-side information while the other three channels damp the negative-capital tail volatility. This is the natural consolidation test with all evidence types pushed at once.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Collateral-Adjusted Leverage Innovation Composite
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is not how much debt an innovator carries but how much debt it carries against liquidatable assets, because intangible-heavy assets cannot support fixed claims; leverage per dollar of non-intangible assets should therefore be the sharper penalty channel.
evaluated.reasoning: The collateral-mismatch ratio delivered a reliable standalone FF5 alpha (-3.6%, t=-3.08) but no cross-sectional slope, exactly the profile of a channel that is informative in the tail and should be used as a component rather than a sort. Swapping it for plain leverage in the winning composite isolates one design choice — how the debt burden of intangible firms should be scaled — while holding the R&D, margin and dilution channels fixed.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Industry-Neutral Margin-Funded Innovation
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at)), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: R&D intensity and gross margin levels are largely technology-and-industry determined, so the informative comparison is whether a firm out-innovates and out-earns its own peers while not diluting; the financing decision, by contrast, is firm-specific and needs no industry adjustment.
evaluated.reasoning: The strongest composite's alpha t-stat (3.45) still lags its FMB slope (5.86), the signature of residual sector concentration in the long leg that FF5 partially prices; neutralizing only the two industry-driven channels should raise the alpha t-stat and Sharpe without diluting the cross-sectional slope. Gen 1's industry test was informative but was applied to a weaker, issuance-based base and to both channels indiscriminately.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Total Intangible Capital Efficiency Composite
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), ADD(ceq, ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: If the capital-efficiency premium reflects mismeasured intangible capital generally, then adding purchased intangibles to the internally generated knowledge stock should strengthen it; if instead the premium is specific to internally generated R&D, adding acquired intangibles will weaken it because acquired intangibles were bought at market prices.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the key remaining economic question in the theme — internally generated versus purchased intangibles — tested inside the best-performing structure so the answer is not confounded by construction differences. The archive's evidence that goodwill-heavy levered firms underperform suggests acquired intangibles behave differently, and this cleanly quantifies how much they cost the signal.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Leverage In Excess Of Intangible Base
evaluated.expression: SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms whose debt ranking far exceeds their intangible-capital ranking have a capital structure mismatched to their asset base — hard claims against soft or scarce assets — and earn low returns as that mismatch is resolved through distress or asset sales.
evaluated.reasoning: Every prior bearish construction either used flows absorbed by the FF5 investment factor, or produced zero mass and nan portfolios; a plain difference of two cross-sectional ranks is continuous, fully covered, and monotone by construction, which is the missing ingredient for aligning the FMB slope with the alpha. It also tests the short side of the theme with the same measurement conventions as the winning long side, making the two directly comparable.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Persistent Innovation Commitment Without Dilution
evaluated.hypothesis: Sustained willingness to report R&D year after year is a commitment signal distinct from the size of the R&D budget: firms that have maintained an innovation program for five consecutive years while funding it from margins and without issuing shares own durable, underpriced knowledge capital.
evaluated.reasoning: The intangible channel has so far been measured only by intensity or cumulative spend, both of which load on the same fast-growing tech firms; reporting persistence is a low-variance, scale-free measure of commitment that should tilt the long leg toward established innovators and could improve the Sharpe of the spread. Combining it with the margin and dilution channels holds the financing side fixed so the test is about the intangible measurement concept alone.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Balanced Commitment And Intensity Composite
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Innovation commitment (a five-year unbroken R&D record) and innovation scale (R&D per dollar of assets) are complementary descriptions of intangible capital, and combining both with margin funding and no dilution identifies durable, self-financed innovators most precisely.
evaluated.reasoning: Persistence and intensity have each been the 50%-weight channel in a winning composite, but never together, and they select different firms — persistence favors established programs, intensity favors high-burn ones. The balanced nesting gives all four channels equal 25% weight, which should retain the FMB slope of the persistence version while restoring the alpha magnitude of the intensity version.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Dilution-Weighted Innovation Quality
evaluated.hypothesis: If the interaction is genuinely about *financing* rather than about innovation quality alone, then giving the financing channel the dominant weight should strengthen the spread; the intangible and margin channels then act as qualifiers identifying which non-diluting firms actually have innovation to protect.
evaluated.reasoning: Every archive composite has placed an intangible measure in the dominant 50%-weight slot and the financing measure at 25% or less, so the relative importance of the two themes has never been tested. This isolates the weighting design choice while holding the three channels fixed, and its outcome tells the final generations whether to lead with financing or with intangibles.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Commitment With Capital-Efficient Knowledge Stock
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(ceq, ADD(dltt, dlc))), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm that has innovated continuously for five years, has built a large knowledge stock per dollar of investor-supplied capital, and has not diluted shareholders is the purest case of productive intangible financing: durable innovation obtained cheaply and owned outright.
evaluated.reasoning: The capital-efficiency channel owns the archive's highest Sharpe but is non-monotone standalone, while persistence owns the highest FMB slope and best Sharpe among composites; pairing them substitutes efficiency for gross margin in the winning structure to see which "affordability" concept the effect really needs. Persistence in the dominant slot should keep the extreme portfolios populated with real, continuously reporting innovators rather than the near-zero-capital tail.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Stock-Financed Intangible Acquirers
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms whose balance sheets are heavy with goodwill while their share count keeps expanding have bought other companies' intangibles by printing equity — the textbook market-timed issuance case — and they subsequently underperform as the acquired intangibles fail to earn their purchase price.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the theme's sharpest bearish story and has only been tested with sparse cash-flow issuance items inside multiplicative structures that produced zero alpha; the additive combination of a goodwill *level* with the dilution measure that has worked all along is fully covered and monotone. Unlike the mismatch difference, it does not simply mirror the winning long composite, so it can add independent short-side evidence.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Dividend-Validated Persistent Innovation
evaluated.hypothesis: Paying cash dividends while sustaining an uninterrupted R&D program is a costly signal that the intangible investment generates real, distributable cash flow rather than requiring perpetual outside funding; such firms should be underpriced relative to equally innovative firms that retain and issue.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has proxied internal funding capacity only by gross margin (an accounting flow); dividends are an actual cash commitment and constitute a different economic channel, which gen 0 tested only with sparse combined payout items and no innovation-persistence measure. Placed in the same structural slot as gross margin, it cleanly answers whether the effect needs accounting margins or verified cash distribution.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Five-Year Net Issuance And Innovation Commitment
evaluated.hypothesis: Cumulative five-year share-count expansion measures how much of the firm's innovation history was paid for by outside equity, a stock concept that matches the five-year innovation-commitment measure far better than a single year of dilution does.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's financing channel has always been one-year dilution or its three-year average; a five-year cumulative issuance measure is the horizon-consistent counterpart to the five-year intangible measures and is known to be a slower-decaying predictor, which should raise the Sharpe by reducing signal turnover. Comparing it directly with the one-year version of the same composite isolates the financing horizon as the single design change.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Five-Channel Balanced Innovation Financing
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable, self-financed innovation is best identified by combining innovation commitment and scale with margin funding and the two dimensions of outside claims — dilution and debt — because debt and equity financing impose different but equally real constraints on intangible-heavy firms.
evaluated.reasoning: The leverage channel is the only ingredient that has ever pushed alpha above 5% with t above 4, and the persistence-plus-intensity pair is the only one that has delivered FMB near 6 with Sharpe near 0.50; this stacks them in the equal-weight architecture that has proven most stable. Because leverage receives only 12.5% weight here rather than 25%, its monotonicity cost to the cross-sectional slope should be limited while its alpha contribution is retained.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Financing-Half Innovation Quality
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at))), SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Giving the financing theme half the total weight — split between equity dilution and debt burden — and the intangible/funding-capacity theme the other half makes the signal a genuine test of financing conditions among innovators rather than an innovation-quality score with a financing tilt.
evaluated.reasoning: Gen 6 showed that raising the dilution weight to 50% produced the archive's highest Sharpe (0.528) though a smaller alpha, while leverage raises alpha; putting both financing channels together at 50% tests whether the two effects combine rather than trade off. It also directly answers the weighting question left open by gen 6, which matters for the final consolidation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Commitment Plus Capital Efficiency Balanced
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(ceq, ADD(dltt, dlc)))), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The right second intangible channel is not how much a firm spends on R&D relative to assets but how much knowledge stock it has accumulated per dollar of capital investors supplied, because the latter directly measures the productivity of external financing in creating intangible assets.
evaluated.reasoning: Capital efficiency carries the highest standalone Sharpe in the archive (1.11) but is non-monotone alone, and when it was given 50% weight alongside persistence the result was middling (FMB 4.11, SR 0.42); at 25% weight inside the balanced structure its tail volatility should be tamed while its information is kept. Comparing directly against gen 6's intensity-based balanced composite isolates which intangible measure belongs in that slot.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Smoothed-State Innovation Financing Quality
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 3), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: R&D intensity and gross margin are slow-moving structural attributes, so their three-year averages measure the firm's true innovation and funding-capacity state with less accounting noise, while dilution is the genuinely event-like variable that must stay at annual frequency.
evaluated.reasoning: Every fundamental channel so far has used a single fiscal year, which injects transitory accounting variation into portfolio membership and raises turnover; smoothing only the state variables and not the financing event should raise both the cross-sectional slope and the Sharpe if the mechanism is a persistent characteristic. This isolates measurement noise as the design variable, holding weights and channels fixed relative to gen 6's best composite.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Brand And Knowledge Investment Without Dilution
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Advertising builds brand capital that is expensed exactly like R&D and is equally invisible on the balance sheet, so total internally generated intangible investment — R&D plus advertising — is the economically complete measure of what self-financing innovators are building.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has defined intangible investment solely as R&D, which excludes consumer-facing firms whose intangible capital is brand rather than patents and therefore leaves part of the mispricing untested. Adding advertising broadens the long leg beyond technology and pharma, which should reduce sector concentration and lift the Sharpe if brand capital is priced like knowledge capital.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Acquired Growth Without Organic Innovation
evaluated.hypothesis: The overvaluation-driven case is a firm that buys its intangibles, pays for them with newly issued shares, and runs no internal innovation program of its own; such firms have no organic source of future intangible value and underperform once acquisition accounting stops flattering earnings.
evaluated.reasoning: Goodwill plus dilution alone had a strong cross-sectional slope but no FF5 alpha because that spread is spanned by the value and investment factors; adding the absence of a persistent R&D program is an intangible-specific dimension the factors do not price and should convert the slope into abnormal return. It is also the exact economic complement of the winning long leg, giving the theme a coherent two-sided interpretation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Organic Versus Acquired Innovation Balanced
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that grow intangible capital internally through a persistent R&D program, rather than by buying it and booking goodwill, and that fund it from margins without diluting shareholders, hold intangible capital acquired below fair value and are systematically underpriced.
evaluated.reasoning: The organic-versus-acquired axis carried the archive's best short-side evidence (α -3.7%, Sharpe -0.53) yet has never entered a long composite, and it is economically the sharpest statement of the theme: innovation created versus innovation purchased with financing. Replacing the R&D-intensity slot with a goodwill penalty keeps the proven equal-weight four-channel architecture while adding a dimension the FF5 factors do not span.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Smoothed Organic Innovation Financing Composite
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 3), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The best available long signal combines a persistent and sizeable internal R&D program measured as a smoothed state, margin funding capacity, absence of dilution, and a clean balance sheet free of purchased intangibles.
evaluated.reasoning: Smoothing the two fundamental states already improved alpha and Sharpe relative to single-year measurement (α 4.7%, SR 0.479), and the goodwill penalty adds the short-side information that was missing; both changes are additive rather than substitutive, so this is the natural consolidation candidate. Goodwill enters at 12.5% weight so it refines the ranking without letting acquisition accounting dominate portfolio membership.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Six-Channel Innovation Financing Quality
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), SUMRANK(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 3), NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: All six evidence channels identified as informative — innovation persistence, innovation scale, margin funding, absence of purchased intangibles, no dilution, and unused debt capacity — describe distinct reasons intangible financing is productive rather than opportunistic, and their equal-weight combination should dominate any subset.
evaluated.reasoning: Leverage is the one channel that has repeatedly pushed alpha above 5% with t above 4, and goodwill is the one channel with proven factor-orthogonal short-side power; this is the first construction that includes both without starving the dilution channel of weight. If the six-channel version raises alpha while holding FMB near 5, it becomes the final recommended signal.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Parsimonious Organic Innovation Versus Dilution
evaluated.hypothesis: The pure financing-times-intangibles effect is that undiluted, organically innovating firms outperform diluting firms whose intangibles were purchased; profitability is a separate premium and including it may add cross-sectional fit without adding abnormal return.
evaluated.reasoning: Gross margin overlaps FF5's profitability factor, which plausibly explains why margin-heavy composites cap out near 4.5% alpha while margin-free composites with leverage reach 5.3%; dropping it while keeping dilution at 50% weight (the configuration with the archive's best composite Sharpe, 0.528) isolates whether the margin channel is buying FMB fit at the cost of alpha. This also yields the most parsimonious three-channel expression of the theme, which matters for credibility.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Organic Share Of Intangible Capital
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(intan, 0))), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is the composition of a firm's intangible capital, not its level: a high share of internally generated knowledge relative to total intangible capital means the assets were built at cost rather than bought at market prices, and such firms outperform when they are also margin-funded and undiluted.
evaluated.reasoning: This measures the organic-versus-purchased distinction as a bounded composition ratio rather than as two separately ranked levels, which removes the size and industry variation embedded in scaling by assets and cannot be dominated by either component. It is the structurally different way to encode the gen-7 discovery, and comparing it with signal 1 tells us whether composition or separate levels is the better encoding.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Levered Stock-Financed Intangible Acquirers
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), SUMRANK(SUMRANK(GROWTH(csho, 1), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)), NEG(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The worst configuration in the theme is a firm that has bought its intangible base using both new shares and borrowed money while running no internal innovation program: it faces impairment risk, fixed claims, and has no organic pipeline to replace the acquired assets.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-7 bearish signal achieved α -3.7% with Sharpe -0.53 using goodwill, dilution and the absence of R&D; adding the debt-financing channel completes the "both financing sources used to buy intangibles" story and should deepen the alpha, since leverage has independently produced reliable negative alphas in this setting. Keeping the additive rank structure avoids the zero-mass gating that produced degenerate portfolios in gen 4.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Smoothed Organic Versus Acquired Balanced
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))), SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 3), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Productive intangible financing is fully described by four equally weighted conditions: a persistent internal R&D program, an asset base not built from purchased goodwill, a smoothed gross margin able to fund innovation, and no shareholder dilution.
evaluated.reasoning: This joins the archive's best cross-sectional structure (equal 25% weights on persistence, goodwill, margin, dilution; FMB 6.48, SR 0.532) with the one measurement change that reliably lifted alpha (three-year smoothing of the margin state, α 4.7%→5.5% in related composites). Because it changes only the smoothing of an existing channel, it should retain the FMB slope near 6.5 while moving alpha toward the 5.5% frontier.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Dilution-Balanced Five-Channel Organic Innovation
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3), NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)))), SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 3), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Innovation scale and the absence of purchased intangibles are secondary qualifiers, while innovation persistence, funding capacity and the financing decision itself deserve primary weight; a signal built on that hierarchy should maximize both evidence types simultaneously.
evaluated.reasoning: The current best alpha composite starves the dilution channel at 12.5% weight, yet every high-Sharpe result in the archive gave dilution 25% or more, so raising dilution to 25% while keeping the smoothed intensity and goodwill channels at 12.5% each targets the one configuration on the frontier that has not been tried. It isolates weighting alone, holding all five channels and their measurement fixed.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Purchased Intangible Penalty Composite
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at))), SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 3), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The economically correct "acquired intangibles" measure is total booked intangible assets, not goodwill alone, because purchased patents, customer lists and licences were equally bought at market prices with outside financing and equally lack the mispricing that surrounds internally generated knowledge.
evaluated.reasoning: Goodwill has done all the work in the organic-versus-acquired channel so far, but it captures only the residual overpayment component of acquisitions, so this tests whether the effect is about overpayment specifically or about purchased intangibles generally. The answer determines which variable belongs in the final signal and is a clean one-variable substitution against signal 1.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Organic Innovation Minus Acquisition Financing
evaluated.expression: SUB(SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), GROWTH(csho, 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The theme reduces to a single contrast: a firm's organic innovation score minus its acquisition-financing score, where the latter combines purchased goodwill with the share issuance used to pay for it; firms high on the first and low on the second are the productive intangible financiers.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a different architecture from the nested SUMRANK family — an explicit difference between a long-side score and the exact bearish composite that produced α -3.7% and SR -0.53 — so it tests whether the two sides are best combined by differencing rather than by pooling ranks. It also deliberately omits gross margin, which overlaps FF5's profitability factor and appears to cap alpha in the pooled composites.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Flow-Financed Intangible Acquirers
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), SUMRANK(SUMRANK(GROWTH(csho, 1), RATIO(ADD(DELTA(dltt, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), at)), NEG(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms currently raising both equity and debt while holding a goodwill-heavy balance sheet and running no internal R&D program are financing acquisitions of other companies' intangibles in real time, and they underperform as the purchased assets fail to earn their cost.
evaluated.reasoning: The levered version of this signal delivered the archive's deepest alpha (-5.1%, t=-4.33) but its FMB slope fell to -2.67 because the debt *level* is a non-monotone, industry-driven characteristic; replacing it with net debt *issuance* is the same repair that lifted the FMB slope from 0.57 to 2.42 in gen 2. Matching all three financing measures to flows also makes the signal a coherent statement about current financing decisions rather than about accumulated capital structure.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Full-Channel Organic Innovation Financing
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))), SUMRANK(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 3), MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: All six informative dimensions belong in the final signal, but the two that carry the cross-sectional slope — innovation persistence and the absence of purchased goodwill — should carry half the weight, with margin, scale, dilution and leverage sharing the rest.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-8 six-channel version reached the highest alpha in the archive (5.6%, t=4.60) but its FMB slope fell to 3.51 because the leverage level and smoothed intensity dominated the top weights; promoting persistence and goodwill to the 50% block should restore the slope toward 5–6 without giving up the leverage-driven alpha. This is the final consolidation candidate, and comparing it to signals 1 and 2 tells us whether breadth or focus wins.
evaluated.author: proposer

considered.name: Self-Funded R&D Intensity
considered.hypothesis: Intangible investment carried on internal cash flow is credible innovation, whereas equity-funded intangible spending is contaminated by market-timed issuance; the spread between R&D intensity and equity-issuance intensity isolates the productive component and earns positive abnormal returns.
considered.reasoning: R&D intensity alone is a known positive-return characteristic and share issuance alone is a known negative one, but the interaction matters because the same R&D dollar is priced very differently when it is bankrolled by new equity sold at a high valuation. Ranking both channels before differencing makes the two themes comparable in units and keeps the signal robust to scaling outliers. COALESCE treats non-reporting firms as zero R&D, which is the standard economic convention and preserves broad coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Debt-Disciplined Innovation Funding
considered.hypothesis: Among R&D-intensive firms, those tilting external funding toward debt rather than equity are monitored, cash-flow-confident innovators, while equity-tilted R&D funders are exploiting overvaluation; the product of R&D intensity and the debt-minus-equity funding mix identifies productive intangible financing.
considered.reasoning: Debt issuance requires servicing capacity and creditor scrutiny, so it is a costly signal when intangible assets provide little collateral, whereas equity issuance is cheapest precisely when the stock is rich. The multiplicative form makes the funding-mix tilt matter most where intangible investment is large, which is the exact conditioning the economic story requires.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Payout-Backed Knowledge Capital
considered.hypothesis: Firms that simultaneously return capital to shareholders and sustain a large stock of accumulated R&D are signaling that their intangible capital is internally financeable and undervalued; this joint configuration should outperform intangible-heavy firms that must absorb outside capital.
considered.reasoning: Negative net external financing (repurchases plus dividends) is a credible statement that management sees the shares as cheap, and it is most informative when the firm also owns a deep, hard-to-value knowledge stock that markets systematically underprice. Five-year cumulative R&D captures the intangible capital state rather than a single noisy annual flow, and SUMRANK combines the two themes with equal, outlier-resistant weight.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Externally Financed Goodwill Buildup
considered.hypothesis: Purchased intangibles (goodwill) created while the firm is simultaneously raising large amounts of debt and equity reflect overpayment for acquired intangible assets funded by cheap capital, and such firms subsequently underperform.
considered.reasoning: Goodwill is the accounting residual of acquisition prices, so its growth is a direct measure of how much the buyer paid above identifiable value; when that purchase is financed externally rather than from internal cash, agency and market-timing motives dominate and later write-downs follow. The multiplicative form is essential because organic goodwill-light growth or financing unaccompanied by acquisitions carries no such implication.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Issuance Against Fading Intangible Productivity
considered.hypothesis: Equity issuance is overvaluation-driven rather than investment-driven when the revenue productivity of the firm's existing intangible base is deteriorating; issuers with declining sales-per-intangible-dollar should earn the most negative subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: If intangible capital is still converting into revenue at an improving rate, new equity plausibly funds a positive-NPV innovation pipeline, but a multi-year decline in intangible productivity means the firm is capitalizing soft assets that no longer generate sales while tapping the market. The five-year TREND supplies the needed state-deterioration concept that a one-year change would measure too noisily, and the product form makes the productivity trend bite only where issuance is actually occurring.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Direction-Signed External Intangible Funding
considered.hypothesis: The same amount of external capital raised is good news when intangible investment intensity is rising (funds are being deployed into innovation) and bad news when intangible intensity is falling (funds are being raised opportunistically), so signing financing volume by the direction of R&D intensity separates productive from timed issuance.
considered.reasoning: This directly implements the economic story as a sign-switch rather than an additive blend: identical financing intensity maps to opposite predictions depending on whether the intangible investment program is expanding or contracting. Using SIGN of the change in R&D-to-sales avoids letting the magnitude of a volatile ratio dominate, while the ranked financing intensity supplies the economically meaningful scale of the interaction.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Dilution-Adjusted R&D Intensity
considered.hypothesis: Intangible investment sustained without shareholder dilution is productive innovation, whereas intangible spending accompanied by share-count expansion reflects market-timed equity funding; measuring dilution from shares outstanding rather than the cash-flow-statement issuance item captures the same economics for the whole cross-section.
considered.reasoning: The gen-0 winner used the same rank-difference logic but was restricted to firms reporting sstk, capping coverage at 0.127 and thinning the extreme portfolios, which is the most likely cause of its weak alpha t-stat relative to its 4.8 FMB t-stat. Share-count growth is available for essentially all firms and captures all dilution channels (secondary offerings, equity-financed deals, option exercise), so this isolates the coverage design choice while holding the mechanism fixed.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Industry-Neutral Self-Funded Innovation
considered.hypothesis: Within an industry, the firm that funds its intangible program internally rather than through equity and debt issuance is the one whose innovation is genuinely value-creating; across industries the same comparison mostly reproduces sector R&D norms and financing conventions, which FF5 factors already span.
considered.reasoning: The gen-0 winner's large FMB slope but weak FF5 alpha t-stat suggests the long-short leg was a pharma/tech versus financials-utilities bet whose systematic component is absorbed by the factor model. Ranking both themes inside industry should preserve the cross-sectional slope while converting it into a cleaner, better-diversified spread, and it also tests total external financing (equity plus debt) rather than equity alone.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Net-Financing-Free Knowledge Capital
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(dltt, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), at))))
considered.hypothesis: A deep accumulated knowledge stock that was built while both equity and debt financing were shrinking identifies self-financing innovators whose intangible capital the market underprices; the same knowledge stock built on simultaneous equity and debt expansion reflects externally subsidized, overvaluation-driven investment.
considered.reasoning: Gen-0's Payout-Backed Knowledge Capital tested the same idea but proxied "no external funding" with repurchases and dividends, which selects large mature payers and gave a negative alpha; net changes in shares and in total debt measure contraction of external capital directly and include young non-payers. Five-year cumulative R&D captures the intangible state rather than a noisy annual flow, and equal-weight nested SUMRANK avoids the multiplicative structures that failed in gen 0.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Intangible Capital Delivered Per Share
considered.hypothesis: The only intangible investment that matters to an incumbent shareholder is the amount surviving dilution, so growth in intangible capital per share separates financing that actually bought innovation from financing that merely transferred claims; firms increasing intangible capital per share earn positive abnormal returns.
considered.reasoning: This changes the interaction from an additive comparison of two ranks to a single per-share intensity, so the financing theme enters as the deflator of the intangible theme rather than as a competing score — a structurally different test of the same story. Combining booked intangibles with three-year cumulative R&D gives one economically complete intangible capital measure, and the one-year growth makes the signal about newly delivered capital rather than about the level of R&D intensity.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Externally Financed Intangible Acquisition
considered.hypothesis: Balance-sheet intangibles grow mainly through acquisitions, and when that growth coincides with heavy equity and debt issuance the firm is paying up for other companies' intangibles with cheap outside capital, which predicts subsequent write-downs and low returns.
considered.reasoning: Gen-0's goodwill version had a coherent FMB slope (-2.80) but a dead long-short leg, consistent with the MUL structure making the signal near-zero for the vast majority of firms and leaving the portfolio extremes unstable. Replacing the product with an additive SUMRANK gives a continuous, well-populated score, and using total intangibles rather than goodwill alone broadens the acquired-intangible measure.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Innovation With Unused Debt Capacity
considered.hypothesis: Because intangible assets are poor collateral, an R&D-intensive firm that has chosen to carry little debt retains real financing capacity and is not investing under distress pressure; the market underprices such firms relative to intangible-heavy firms whose innovation is already levered.
considered.reasoning: All prior proposals used financing flows; this one uses the financing state (stock of debt), so it tests whether the interaction operates through capital-structure capacity rather than through the timing of new issues. It also has near-universal coverage because it needs only xrd, dltt, dlc and at, which addresses the sparsity that plagued the flow-based archive.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Triple-Channel Self-Financed Innovation
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Productive intangible financing is identified jointly by three conditions — substantial intangible investment, no shareholder dilution, and unused debt capacity — because a firm meeting all three is funding innovation from internal resources and retains options, while intangible-heavy firms that are both diluting and levered are funding innovation on terms set by outside capital.
considered.reasoning: Dilution and leverage state were the two strongest portfolio channels in gen 1 but were each tested in isolation against R&D intensity; combining them tests whether their information is complementary rather than redundant. Equal-weight nested SUMRANK keeps the additive structure that has worked while ensuring no single channel drives the extreme portfolios, which should stabilize the long-short composition.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Persistently Undiluted Innovation
considered.hypothesis: Whether intangible investment is genuinely self-funded is a multi-year property of financing policy, not a one-year event; R&D-intensive firms with three years of low average dilution are credibly internally financed, while a single clean year can simply reflect issuance timing.
considered.reasoning: This isolates one design choice — the horizon of the financing channel — against the gen-1 winner while holding the intangible channel and the rank-difference structure fixed. If the smoothed version improves both the FMB slope and the alpha t-stat, the mechanism is a persistent financing-policy state; if it degrades, the effect is driven by recent issuance events and future work should stay at annual frequency.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Margin-Funded Innovation
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: The economically relevant question is whether the firm's own gross margin can pay for its intangible program; innovators with high gross profitability and no dilution are funding R&D internally, whereas equally R&D-intensive firms with thin margins must sell equity and are the market-timing candidates.
considered.reasoning: The archive has proxied "internal funding" only negatively (absence of issuance), never positively by the firm's actual cash-generating capacity; gross profit is the one internal-funds measure available in the intangibles menu and is known to be the most persistent profitability signal. This tests whether the dilution effect is really a funding-capacity effect, which would explain why pure payout-based proxies in gen 0 failed on old, low-growth firms.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Knowledge Growth Versus Equity Base Growth
considered.hypothesis: When accumulated knowledge capital grows faster than the book equity base, incremental capital is being converted into innovation; when book equity grows faster than knowledge capital, the firm is absorbing outside funding that is not producing intangible assets.
considered.reasoning: This changes the financing measure from share count to the book equity base, which aggregates issuance, retained earnings and buybacks into the total capital the firm must earn a return on, and it puts both themes in growth-rate space rather than comparing a flow to a level. It is the natural cross-sectionally rankable version of gen 1's per-share intangible capital idea, which had a strong alpha (t=2.85) but an uninformative FMB slope due to raw-growth outliers.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Levered Purchased-Intangible Balance Sheet
considered.hypothesis: A balance sheet that is simultaneously heavy in goodwill and heavy in liabilities embeds unrecognized impairment risk against fixed claims: the acquired intangibles were paid for with borrowed money, and equity holders bear the writedown, so such firms earn low subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: All prior bearish proposals used financing and intangible *flows*, and their spreads were absorbed by the FF5 investment factor, leaving zero alpha despite strong FMB slopes; a levels-based configuration of the same story is much less collinear with asset growth. It also tests the acquired-intangible channel (goodwill) against the internally-generated channel (R&D) that has been dominating, which is the key economic distinction in the theme.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Innovation Minus Net Debt Issuance
considered.hypothesis: Intangible investment funded by fresh borrowing is a leveraged bet on soft assets that cannot be liquidated, so R&D intensity net of contemporaneous net debt issuance identifies innovation the firm can actually sustain through a funding shock.
considered.reasoning: Gen 1 showed the debt channel produces the largest alpha (4.5%) but almost no cross-sectional slope when measured as a leverage *level*, which suggests the level is a noisy, industry-driven proxy; the annual net-issuance *flow* is the decision variable and should restore the FMB slope if the mechanism is about funding choices rather than static capital structure. Paired with signal 1, this tells us whether to build later refinements on debt stocks or debt flows.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Four-Channel Internally Financed Innovation
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))))
considered.hypothesis: Productive intangible financing requires both the ability to pay (gross margin) and the absence of outside claims on the innovation (no dilution, little debt); stacking funding capacity with funding claims should identify self-financing innovators more sharply than either enhancement alone.
considered.reasoning: Gross margin raised the cross-sectional slope while leverage state raised the alpha, and the two describe distinct economics — internal cash generation versus who owns the claim on it — so they are unlikely to be redundant. This is the direct consolidation test of the archive's two best refinements and will tell us which axis to keep in the final signal.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Knowledge Capital Per Dollar Of Investor Capital
considered.hypothesis: The efficiency with which supplied outside capital has been converted into an accumulated knowledge stock is the cleanest measure of productive intangible financing: firms holding a large R&D stock per dollar of equity plus debt capital have built innovation cheaply, while firms with little knowledge stock per financed dollar absorbed capital without creating intangible assets.
considered.reasoning: Every archive winner compares two separately ranked channels; this instead deflates the intangible stock by the total capital investors have actually committed, so the interaction is structural rather than additive and is not mechanically an R&D-intensity sort. Five-year cumulative R&D matches the stock concept in the denominator, and winsorizing controls the small-capital-base outliers that destroyed the FMB slope of the gen-1 per-share version.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Undiluted Innovation Acceleration
considered.hypothesis: A firm ramping up R&D intensity while keeping its share count flat is committing internal resources to a newly attractive opportunity set, whereas a firm ramping R&D on the back of new shares is spending other people's money raised at a favorable price.
considered.reasoning: Every successful archive signal measures the intangible theme as a *level* of intensity, which risks being an R&D-premium restatement; this isolates the intangible-channel flow while holding the financing channel and rank-difference structure fixed. If the growth version retains the alpha, the mechanism is about new investment decisions rather than about static innovation intensity, which matters for how we build the final signal.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Dilution By Cash-Burning Innovators
considered.hypothesis: The overvaluation-driven issuance case is concentrated in firms whose R&D spending exceeds their entire gross profit: these firms cannot self-fund, so heavy dilution reflects a window of favorable pricing rather than a validated investment program, and they underperform.
considered.reasoning: The archive's bearish signals have failed because they sorted the whole cross-section on flows that FF5's investment factor spans; this instead switches on a hard economic solvency condition (R&D above gross profit) and only then reads dilution, which targets exactly the population where market timing is feasible. The indicator makes it a true conditional rather than the multiplicative rank blends that failed in gen 0, because the gate is a discrete state, not a second ranked score.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Debt Against Non-Intangible Collateral
considered.hypothesis: Leverage is only as safe as the liquidatable assets behind it; firms whose debt is large relative to assets excluding booked intangibles have financed soft, non-collateralizable assets with hard claims and bear elevated distress and impairment risk, earning low returns.
considered.reasoning: This repairs the gen-2 levered-goodwill failure by replacing an additive composite of two levels — whose relation to returns was non-monotone (FMB t=+0.60) — with a single continuous collateral-coverage ratio that should be monotone across the cross-section. It is also economically the mirror of the winning long side: intangible assets are attractive when equity-financed and dangerous when debt-financed.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Innovation With Stable Financing Policy
considered.hypothesis: Innovators whose share count follows a smooth path are funding intangible investment from a stable internal source, while innovators with volatile dilution are opportunistically tapping equity markets whenever conditions permit, which signals dependence on sentiment rather than on project quality.
considered.reasoning: The archive has measured the financing channel only by the level or three-year average of dilution; the second moment is a distinct economic concept — reliance on episodic market access — and may capture market timing that averages out in the mean. Keeping the same rank-difference structure isolates this new financing statistic against the established R&D-intensity channel.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rank-Stabilized Knowledge Capital Efficiency
considered.hypothesis: Firms that have accumulated a large knowledge stock per dollar of investor-supplied capital have converted external financing into innovation efficiently and are underpriced; the economic content is the ordering of this efficiency, not the extreme magnitudes of the raw ratio.
considered.reasoning: This is a deliberate diagnostic on gen 3's outsized result: a monotone rank transform preserves the economic ordering while removing the influence of near-zero and negative capital denominators, so comparing the two tells us whether the 54.5% alpha is a genuine efficiency premium or a magnitude artifact of a few tail firms. It should simultaneously repair the weak FMB slope, since the cross-sectional regression is then run on a bounded regressor.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Knowledge Stock Against Total Claims
considered.hypothesis: Intangible capital that dwarfs the firm's total outside claims represents innovation the shareholders own outright, whereas a small knowledge stock relative to large liabilities means the financing raised went to obligations rather than to innovation.
considered.reasoning: Total liabilities is strictly positive for essentially all firms, so this variant of the capital-efficiency mechanism cannot flip sign or explode the way an equity-plus-debt denominator can, isolating the robustness of the denominator choice. If the alpha and Sharpe of the gen-3 ratio largely survive here, the mechanism is real; if it collapses, the earlier result was driven by negative-equity distress cases.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Capital-Efficient Innovation With Margins
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(ceq, ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: The strongest form of productive intangible financing combines three properties: a knowledge stock built cheaply relative to capital supplied, gross margins able to sustain it, and no need for fresh dilution; each addresses a different reason a high R&D stock might be unprofitable.
considered.reasoning: The two best-performing families in the archive — the capital-efficiency ratio (highest alpha and Sharpe) and the margin-plus-dilution composite (highest FMB slope, t=5.48) — have never been combined, and SUMRANK ranks the ratio internally so its tail behavior cannot dominate the score. This is the consolidation candidate that could deliver strong cross-sectional and portfolio evidence at once.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Successfully Funded Constrained Innovators
considered.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(SUB(COALESCE(xrd, 0), SUB(sale, cogs)), 0), SUMRANK(GROWTH(csho, 1), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms whose R&D exceeds their entire gross profit, access to equity is the binding constraint, so raising capital is a certification event: heavily R&D-intensive burners that succeed in funding themselves outperform, because the alternative is curtailing innovation.
considered.reasoning: Gen 3 tested this exact population expecting underperformance and got the opposite (alpha +2.4%, t=2.06, Sharpe 0.79), which is direct evidence that dilution is good news precisely where internal funds cannot cover intangible investment. This version keeps the discrete solvency gate but scores gated firms on both the amount of funding obtained and the intensity of the innovation being funded, sharpening the certification interpretation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Dilution-Funded Innovation Ramp
